data.name: Los 4 tonos
data.description: El tono cambia completamente el significado

cards.translation:
First tone — high and flat, like singing a steady note
Think of a flat line on a graph
cards.mnemonic: Imagine a tightrope walker balancing perfectly on a high, straight line — no wobble, no dip.

examples.t: mā (妈) = mother — high, calm, like a mother's steady voice
bā (八) = eight — say it like a flat 'baa' from a calm sheep

cards.translation: Second tone — rising, like asking "¿Cómo?" or "What?" in surprise
cards.mnemonic: Picture someone leaning forward and asking '¿Eh?' — your voice goes up like a question mark.

examples.t: má (麻) = hemp / numb — rising like a question about the plant
lái (来) = to come — 'Come here?' with a rising tone

cards.translation: Third tone — dip then rise, like a thoughtful "hmm?" or a rollercoaster valley
cards.mnemonic: Imagine a valley: your voice goes down into the dip, then climbs back up — like saying 'hmm... really?'

examples.t: mǎ (马) = horse — the horse goes down into a valley and back up

cards.translation: Fourth tone — sharp falling, like saying "¡No!" or "Stop!" firmly
cards.mnemonic: Picture a hammer striking down — your voice slams from high to low like a decisive '¡No!'

examples.t: mà (骂) = to scold — scolding with a sharp falling 'ma!'

cards.translation: Neutral tone — light and unstressed, like a soft "lah" at the end of a word
cards.mnemonic: Think of a feather floating down gently — no emphasis, just a light touch at the end.

examples.t: ma (吗) = question particle — 'Nǐ hǎo ma?' = 'How are you?'

cards.translation:
Rule: 3rd + 3rd → 2nd + 3rd
When two third tones meet, the first one becomes second tone
cards.mnemonic: Two valleys in a row feel awkward — so the first valley flattens into a rising hill.

examples.t: nǐ hǎo → ní hǎo (你好) — 'hello' — say 'nee how' not 'nee-ee how'

cards.translation: Rule: bù (不) is 4th tone, but before another 4th tone it becomes 2nd tone
cards.mnemonic: The word 'no' softens before another strong 'no' — like saying 'no... no' more gently the second time.

examples.t: bù hǎo (不好) = not good — bù stays 4th
bú shì (不是) = is not — becomes 2nd before shì (4th tone)

cards.translation:
The famous example: mā (mother) má (hemp) mǎ (horse) mà (scold) ma (question)
Same sound, different tone = different meaning!
cards.mnemonic: Context is king — the same 'ma' can mean mother, horse, or scold, so listen to the tone AND the situation.

examples.t: Nǐ de mā qí mǎ — 'Your mother rides a horse'

cards.translation: mother — mom
horse
to scold — to yell at someone
you
good — fine, well
I — me
is — yes (to be)
no — not
to come
question particle — ? (turns a statement into a question)

data.name: Iniciales (consonantes)
data.description: b p m f / d t n l / g k h / j q x / zh ch sh r / z c s

cards.translation: Like English b but without voice — soft 'p'
cards.mnemonic: Think of 'b' as a ball that bounces but doesn't pop — no puff of air.

cards.translation: Like English p — with a puff of air
cards.mnemonic: A puff of air blows out a candle — that's 'p'.

cards.translation: Same as English m — hummed with lips closed
cards.mnemonic: Close your lips and hum — like a mmm of yummy food.

cards.translation: Same as English f — air through teeth
cards.mnemonic: Blow air like ffff — as if cooling soup.

cards.translation: Like English d but without voice — soft 't'
cards.mnemonic: Tap your tongue behind teeth — d is a gentle tap, no explosion.

cards.translation: Like English t — with a puff of air
cards.mnemonic: A t explosion — like saying 't' with a burst of air.

cards.translation: Same as English n — tip of tongue on ridge
cards.mnemonic: Hum through your nose — n like 'n' in 'no'.

cards.translation: Same as English l — tongue tip touches roof
cards.mnemonic: Light l — like 'l' in 'love'.

cards.translation: Like English g but without voice — soft 'k'
cards.mnemonic: G like go — but no vibration in throat.

cards.translation: Like English k — with a puff of air
cards.mnemonic: A k like 'k' in 'kite' — with a burst of air.

cards.translation: Like English h but deeper — a breathy rasp
cards.mnemonic: Fog a window with your breath — h like 'h' in 'hot'.

cards.translation: Like English j but softer — no 'd' sound
cards.mnemonic: A jeep starting — but with a soft 'j'.

cards.translation: Like English ch but with a puff of air
cards.mnemonic: Say 'cheese' — but q with a strong burst of air.

cards.translation: Like English sh but with a smile — between 's' and 'sh'
cards.mnemonic: A sh with a smile — like saying 'she' but with a grin.

cards.translation: Like English j but with tongue curled back — retroflex
cards.mnemonic: Curl your tongue back like a snake — 'zh' as in 'j' but with a twist.

cards.translation: Like English ch but with tongue curled back and puff of air
cards.mnemonic: A chug of a train — with a burst of air.

cards.translation: Like English sh but with tongue curled back
cards.mnemonic: Curl your tongue back and say sh — like 'shh' but deeper.

cards.translation: Like English r but with a buzzing sound — tongue curled back
cards.mnemonic: A buzz like a bee — but with your tongue curled.

cards.translation: Like English ds in 'kids' — but without voice
cards.mnemonic: A buzz like a bee — but with a 'z' sound.

cards.translation: Like English ts in 'cats' — with a puff of air
cards.mnemonic: A tsunami — 'ts' with a burst of air.

cards.translation: Same as English s — a hissing sound
cards.mnemonic: A snake hisses — 'sss'.

cards.translation: Eight — lucky number in Chinese
He or she — gender-neutral pronoun
Good — one of the most useful words
Please — polite request

examples.n: May I ask, what's your name?

cards.translation: Eat — essential verb
Three — number

data.name: Finales (vocales y nasales)
data.description: a o e i u ü — simples, diptongos y nasales

cards.translation: Vowel a — like “ah” in father
cards.mnemonic: A tall letter with a flat top — like a mountain peak, say 'ah' as if opening your mouth wide.

examples.t: a is the basis for many finals: ai, ao, an

examples.n: Remember the tone: high and flat.

cards.translation: Vowel o — like “aw” in law (but with rounded lips)
cards.mnemonic: A circle — pucker your lips as if blowing a bubble, say 'oh'.

cards.translation: Vowel e — like “uh” in but, but with a neutral tongue position
cards.mnemonic: A flat line — keep your tongue flat and say 'uh' as if hesitating.

examples.t: In en, it sounds like 'un' as in rén (person)

cards.translation: Vowel i — like “ee” in see
cards.mnemonic: A straight line with a dot — like a needle, say 'ee' with a smile.

examples.n: Remember the tone: high and level.

cards.translation: Vowel u — like “oo” in food
cards.mnemonic: A cup shape — like a cup, round your lips and say 'oo'.

cards.translation: Vowel ü — like “ü” in German, or “ee” with rounded lips
cards.mnemonic: A 'u' with two dots — like a surprised face, pucker your lips and say 'ee'.

examples.t: After j, q, x, y, the dots are dropped: ju is actually jü

cards.translation: Compound final ai — like “eye” in time
cards.mnemonic: A + i — glide from 'ah' to 'ee', like saying 'eye' quickly.

cards.translation: Compound final ei — like “ay” in say
cards.mnemonic: e + i — say 'eh' then 'ee', like the English word 'hey' without the 'h'.

cards.translation: Compound final ao — like “ow” in cow
cards.mnemonic: a + o — from 'ah' to 'oh', like saying 'ow' when you bump your head.

cards.translation: Compound final ou — like “oh” in go
cards.mnemonic: o + u — round your lips and say 'oh', like realizing something.

cards.translation: Compound final ia — like “ya” in yard
cards.mnemonic: i + a — glide from 'ee' to 'ah', like saying 'ya'.

cards.translation: Compound final ie — like “ye” in yes
cards.mnemonic: i + e — say 'ee' then 'eh', like 'yeh'.

cards.translation: Compound final ua — like “wa” in water
cards.mnemonic: u + a — round your lips and say 'wah'.

cards.translation: Compound final uo — like “wo” in wonder
cards.mnemonic: u + o — glide from 'oo' to 'oh', like saying 'wo'.

cards.translation: Compound final üe — like “üe” with rounded lips, similar to “wet” but with rounded lips
cards.mnemonic: ü + e — pucker your lips and say 'yeh', like blowing a kiss.

cards.translation: Nasal final an — like “an” in can
cards.mnemonic: a + n — say 'ah' and then let your tongue touch the roof for the 'n'.

cards.translation: Nasal final en — like “un” in sun
cards.mnemonic: e + n — say 'uh' and then 'n', like the English word 'un' but shorter.

cards.translation: Nasal final in — like “in” in sin
cards.mnemonic: i + n — say 'ee' and then 'n', like the English word 'in'.

cards.translation: Nasal final un — like “wun” in wonder but shorter
cards.mnemonic: u + n — say 'oo' then 'n', like 'wun'.

cards.translation: Nasal final ang — like “ahng” in long (with a nasal 'ng')
cards.mnemonic: a + ng — say 'ah' and then let the air come out your nose, like a humming sound.

cards.translation: Nasal final eng — like “ung” in hung but with a neutral vowel
cards.mnemonic: e + ng — say 'uh' and then 'ng', like the end of 'song'.

cards.translation: Nasal final ing — like “ing” in sing
cards.mnemonic: i + ng — say 'ee' and then 'ng', like the English word 'sing'.

cards.translation: Nasal final ong — like “ung” in young
cards.mnemonic: o + ng — round your lips and say 'oh' then 'ng', like 'ong'.

cards.translation: Special final er — like “er” in her (American English)
cards.mnemonic: e + r — curl your tongue back, like saying 'er' with a retroflex r.

cards.translation: cat — māo uses the final ao
good, well — hǎo uses the final ao
dog — gǒu uses the final ou
home, family — jiā uses the final ia
The character for you — left side is a person (亻), right side is a hook. Pronounced with a falling-rising tone (third tone).
cards.mnemonic: The right side looks like a person leaning forward to ask 'you?' with a rising question mark shape.

examples.t: 你好 — the most common greeting in Chinese.
Tone tip: say 'nee' then drop and rise your voice like a question.

cards.translation: The character for I/me — the left side is a hand (扌), the right side is a spear. Pronounced with a falling-rising tone.
cards.mnemonic: A hand holding a spear — 'I' am the one holding the weapon.

examples.t: 我是学生 — I am a student.
Tone tip: 'wo' starts low, dips lower, then rises.

cards.translation: The character for to be (am/is/are) — the top looks like a sun (日), bottom is a footprint. Pronounced with a falling tone.
cards.mnemonic: The sun (日) stepping forward — 'is' = the sun IS there.

examples.t: 我是老师 — I am a teacher.
Tone tip: 'shir' — say it flat and firm, like a command.

cards.translation: The character for good — left is a woman (女), right is a child (子). Woman + child = good. Pronounced with a falling-rising tone.
cards.mnemonic: A woman with her child — that's a good picture!

examples.n: The most useful word in Chinese

examples.t: Tone tip: 'how' — start high, dip down, come back up.

cards.translation: Hello — literally 'you good'. The most essential greeting.
Thank you — the character repeats for emphasis. Both syllables have a falling tone.

examples.n: Adding 你 makes it more personal

cards.translation: Sorry — literally 'not able to face you'. The middle syllable is neutral tone.

examples.t: 对不起！ — Excuse me! (when bumping into someone)

cards.translation: I / me — one of the first pronouns to learn.
You — essential for addressing someone directly.
He / him — the person radical (亻) on the left. Same pronunciation as 她 (she).
She / her — the woman radical (女) on the left. Same sound as 他 (he).
We / us — 我 (I) + 们 (plural marker). The 们 is neutral tone.
To be (am/is/are) — the linking verb. Falling tone.
Is not — negation of 是. The 不 changes to second tone before a fourth tone.
To have — the character looks like a hand holding something. Third tone.
Don't have — negation of 有. Very common in everyday speech.
Good / well — woman + child = good. Third tone.
Not good — negation of 好. Simple and direct.
Big — a person stretching their arms wide. Fourth tone.
Small / little — three small strokes. Third tone.
To come — the character shows a person arriving. Second tone.
To go — the character shows a person leaving. Fourth tone.
To eat — the left radical means mouth (口). First tone.
To drink — mouth radical (口) on the left. First tone.
To speak / to say — the left radical means words/speech (讠). First tone.
